newsitem.title: USA: US FCC likely act on digital TV standard this year.
newsitem.headline: US FCC likely act on digital TV standard this year.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission looks set to approve by year's end the new high-definition digital television standard agreed to by the TV, computer and consumer electronic industries.

A day after representatives from the computer, TV and consumer electronics industries agreed on the broadcast standard, FCC officials Tuesday praised the development and sought speedy agency approval. The agreement expires Dec. 31.
The commissioners are expected to act on the measure individually rather than together at a public meeting.
"A month ought to be enough time to get this voted by circulation," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told reporters, referring to the private voting method.

While the accord between the computer, broadcast and consumer electronics industries calls on the FCC to issue a broadcast transmission standard, the agency would not mandate key aspects of digital TV technology.
Instead, the eventual shape of the TV screen and the technology for putting images on to the screen would be dictated by the market -- and not a government agency.
Other FCC commissioners praised the pact.
"Prompt adoption of this standard will allow the United States to retain its preeminent global position in advanced digital broadcast technologies," said Commissioner James Quello in a statement.
"I am hopeful that we will be able to promptly conclude that this compromise will serve the public interest," said Commissioner Rachelle Chong in a statement.
